Vendored Tree-sitter runtime (syntax highlighting for the sketerm editor
pane). MIT, GPL-3-compatible.

`zig build` compiles this runtime and the grammars into the GUI targets
only (see `addTreeSitter` in build.zig). None of it may ever enter the
`sketerm-mux` / `mux-portable` dependency graph.

runtime
  github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter @ 97e2eeb83cdd6d78d7a614318abf9dead59acace (2026-08-04)
  MIT (LICENSE) - lib/include/tree_sitter/api.h + lib/src/**
  lib/src/lib.c is the upstream amalgamation (#includes every other .c).
  lib/src/wasm/ was dropped: wasm_store.c compiles to stubs without
  TREE_SITTER_FEATURE_WASM, which we never define.
  lib/src/unicode/ is ICU-derived (lib/src/unicode/LICENSE, permissive).

grammars
  NOT in this repository. src/editor/grammars.zig pins each upstream
  grammar repository by commit and by the SHA-256 of its GitHub archive
  tarball; build.zig (`fetchGrammar`) downloads and unpacks each archive
  into the Zig build cache the first time a step that compiles it runs,
  and fails the build on a checksum mismatch. The archives already carry
  the generated src/parser.c, so no node/JS toolchain is involved. They
  are all MIT; tree-sitter-lua ships its license as LICENSE.md.

  Adding a grammar is: one `Upstream` member with its pin (compute the
  checksum with `curl -sSL <archive url> | sha256sum`), one `Grammar`
  member, its `Query` members, and the language that uses it in
  src/editor/languages.zig.

  Each grammar keeps ITS OWN src/tree_sitter/ headers as upstream ships
  them rather than sharing one copy: those headers pin the language ABI
  the generated table was emitted against (v14 or v15), and the runtime
  accepts anything in [TREE_SITTER_MIN_COMPATIBLE_LANGUAGE_VERSION 13, 15].

queries
  Each `Query` in src/editor/grammars.zig is an upstream highlights file
  of the pinned commit, embedded into the binary by build.zig as
  `ts_query_<name>`. Which queries a grammar concatenates (C++ on top of
  C, TypeScript on top of JavaScript, as upstream's tree-sitter.json
  does) is `Grammar.queries`. Capture names are the nvim-flavoured
  convention; src/editor/syntax.zig maps them onto a small fixed palette
  of highlight kinds, and a test fails on any capture a pinned query uses
  that the palette does not place.

Measured and not added: Ruby (tree-sitter/tree-sitter-ruby @
ad907a69da0c, 15 MB parser.c, ~3 s to compile, 2 MB of binary; the cost
table for every grammar is in docs/editor-commands.md). Ruby, like every
language without a grammar, still gets comment toggling, string-aware
bracket matching and folding from its row in src/editor/languages.zig.
